Keywords: Danylo Polish campaigns and Yotvingian resistance
RagShortTexts: Danylo and Polish princes campaigned in Yotvingian lands.
Frontier security, tribute and alliances shaped the campaigns.

Variants.Content: Danylo and Polish princes campaigned among Yotvingian groups for security, tribute and recognition. Local groups resist, negotiate or withdraw; receiving tribute once does not put every woodland settlement under equal control.
Yotvingian woodland campaigning requires attention to side tracks and return routes. Tribute and captives slow the column; rear protection competes with the advance for manpower.
Polish partners need agreed aims and shares. A local leader’s promise does not bind every neighboring group, so continued tribute collection requires identifiable parties.
Frontier households fear raids and campaigning armies consuming stores. Return to fields, recovered animals and reopened exchange matter more immediately than distant declarations of pacification.
